body:
Parent: #737

## Description

Retain usable child payload fields from native sub-issue listing and task-list fallback GETs. Prove native field availability with a captured fixture before removing fallback fetches.

## Evidence and ownership

**Stop refetching GitHub children the list call already returned.** [`sub_issues`](https://github.com/Falconiere/toolu/blob/e829adda0b889830e49d13fe86ff7934f2501ecc/crates/epic-orchestrator/src/tracker/github_fetch.rs#L73) keeps title, state, and URL and drops the rest of each list item. [`details`](https://github.com/Falconiere/toolu/blob/e829adda0b889830e49d13fe86ff7934f2501ecc/crates/epic-orchestrator/src/tracker/github_fetch.rs#L106) then GETs the issue again for body and labels, plus `blocked_by` and a closing-PR query. The task-list fallback GETs each referenced issue inside `sub_issues`, and `details` GETs that same path again. This pass did not capture a fixture proving the native sub-issues payload includes `body` and `labels`; the task-list double GET does not depend on that. A rate limit must still fail the build rather than drop native blockers. `deps_source` and the four-way fetch concurrency stay.

Source baseline: `6047c50edd68860b775aa1e87d52d1303c70eb93`. Source findings are not runtime proof; reproduce the relevant failure or measure the baseline before claiming a fix or speedup.

## Priority and dependencies

3 — Measured performance.

None; can be delivered independently within the priority order.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Task-list children reuse the issue GET already performed rather than fetching that same issue again for body/labels.
- [ ] Capture and sanitize a real native sub-issues response; reuse body/labels only when available, and fetch missing details when fields are absent.
- [ ] Preserve pagination, ordering/dedup, four-way fetch concurrency, closing-PR lookup, and native+text/text deps_source behavior.
- [ ] A dependency API rate limit still fails graph construction rather than dropping native blockers; distinguish unsupported API from failure and record request-count savings.

## Test scenarios

1. Replay a captured native payload with body/labels through a real loopback server: no redundant detail GET; correct excerpts/labels/blockers/PRs.
2. Replay payloads with omitted/null detail fields: required fallback GETs still occur and no details silently disappear.
3. For task-list fallback and paginated native lists, count requests and assert one issue detail fetch per referenced child, correct dedup, and concurrency <=4.
4. Return rate limits and unsupported-dependency statuses separately: rate limits fail, unsupported API uses documented text fallback. Extend tracker/tests/github_fetch_test.rs.

## Verification and scope boundaries

- Implementation uses native Rust and the real binary, Git, ast-grep, subprocesses, and local HTTP/Unix servers as appropriate. Use isolated temporary repositories/config roots and existing shared fixtures; no mocking crates or ignored tests.
- Add focused regression coverage in the owning crate and run its tests plus `cargo xtask gate` before pushing an implementation. Record actual commands/results; do not replace verification with a Jev judgment or suppress gate failures.
- For performance/resource work, attach reproducible before/after release-build results with workload, platform, sample count, and relevant request/scan/parse/allocation/thread/fd counts. Do not invent speedup targets from this source audit.
- Preserve public behavior except deliberate documented idempotency/status contract changes. Follow CLI compatibility and generated-document checks if those surfaces change.
- This issue was created as specification only. No implementation, fault injection, benchmarks, or heap profiling were executed while writing it.
title: perf(epic): reuse fetched GitHub child issue details
